steps.name: Normalize counts and VST for pathway scoring
steps.question: Given the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 UC inflamed vs 6 control), what is a variance-stabilized expression matrix suitable as input to GSVA, and does sample_01's low library size distort normalization?
acceptance_criteria: counts.csv and metadata.csv are loaded and sample order/labels are matched between them
raw counts are size-factor normalized and variance-stabilized (e.g., DESeq2 vst or varianceStabilizingTransformation) producing a genes x samples continuous-valued matrix
a library size / normalization diagnostic (e.g., size factors, PCA or boxplot of normalized counts) is produced flagging sample_01 as the low-depth outlier without removing it
the VST matrix is saved with gene symbols as rownames for downstream use

steps.name: GSVA hallmark pathway activity scoring
steps.question: What is the per-sample GSVA activity score for each of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways, computed from the VST-normalized colon expression matrix (6 UC inflamed vs 6 control)?
acceptance_criteria: the human Hallmark gene set collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols) is loaded from the staged MSigDB hallmark GMT and matched to gene symbols in the VST matrix, reporting how many hallmark genes are found in the 12000-gene panel
GSVA is run with the VST-normalized matrix and the hallmark gene sets producing a 50 pathways x 12 samples activity score matrix
the pathway x sample score matrix is exported as a CSV, one row per sample present in metadata.csv, so every sample has a full set of 50 hallmark scores
if fewer than ~5 genes of a hallmark set are present in the data that set's score is flagged as low-confidence rather than silently reported

steps.name: Differential hallmark pathway activity: UC inflamed vs control
steps.question: Which of the 50 Hallmark pathways show significantly different GSVA activity scores between the 6 UC-inflamed and 6 control colon samples?
acceptance_criteria: a per-pathway two-group comparison (moderated t-test via limma, or Welch t-test with BH-FDR correction) is run on the GSVA score matrix comparing UC inflamed vs control as defined in metadata.csv
output table lists all 50 pathways with effect size (mean difference or logFC-like statistic), raw p-value and adjusted p-value (FDR), sorted by significance

pathways significant at FDR < 0.05 are explicitly called out; if none reach that threshold, the top pathways by nominal p-value are reported with that caveat stated, given the unpaired n=6 vs n=6 design
the result explicitly notes sample_01's low library size as a potential source of noise if it appears as an outlier in the score distribution

steps.name: Heatmap of Hallmark pathway activity across samples
steps.question: What does a heatmap of the 50-pathway GSVA activity score matrix, annotated by UC inflamed vs control status, show about which hallmark pathways separate the two groups?
acceptance_criteria: a clustered heatmap (rows = 50 hallmark pathways, columns = 12 samples) of GSVA scores is produced with a top or side annotation bar coding each sample's condition (UC inflamed vs control) from metadata.csv
rows and/or columns are hierarchically clustered so that condition-driven blocks of pathway activity are visually apparent
pathways found significant (or top-ranked) in the T2S2 differential test are visually highlighted or listed in the figure legend/caption
sample_01 is labeled in the column annotation so its low-depth status is visible when interpreting whether it clusters as an outlier
the figure is saved as a static image file (e.g., PNG/PDF) alongside the underlying score matrix used to draw it

plan.title: GSVA hallmark pathway activity in UC colon
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq raw gene-level counts (12000 genes x 13 samples, but metadata says 12 samples: 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control) from Salmon in human colon. To get a per-sample pathway activity score, raw counts must first be normalized/variance-stabilized (they are not appropriate for GSVA as raw integer counts), then GSVA run against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (available at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt) to produce a sample x pathway activity matrix. That matrix is then visualized as a heatmap annotated by condition (UC inflamed vs control) to show which hallmark pathways separate the two groups, and formally tested (per-pathway t-test / limma) between groups to rank the separating pathways. The library-size outlier (sample_01, ~4x below median) is flagged through normalization diagnostics and heatmap sample ordering rather than silently dropped, since removing a real biological replicate reduces the already-small n=6/6 design.
